_note: Criteria judged from the reference list after the citation check (V-098). A criterion matches a strategy by its own level descriptors, never by its name: at least min_levels of its levels must match one of the strategy's patterns. The first matching strategy wins.
_types_note: Provider type tags (app/external/work_type.py) grouped into classes. A tag in no class makes an identified work 'other': it counts neither as a major reference nor as an internet site.
_confirmed_note: Only a lookup whose identity was confirmed says what the entry is.
_web_note: An entry no catalogue identified, that gives a web address and says it was retrieved or accessed online, is counted as an internet site.
_text_types_note: An entry no catalogue confirmed is typed from its own citation text, in this order; the first class with a matching pattern wins. Repository and preprint entries count neither as major references nor as internet sites. A wrong 'major' only keeps the counts from lowering a grade, so the journal, conference and book cues may be broad; the web typing is the one that can lower a grade, so it is kept narrow. An entry no rule types stays unidentified.
_isbn_note: An unconfirmed entry whose parsed record carries an ISBN, and no repository cue, is a book.
_web_scholarly_note: Web typing needs a web cue and an address in the entry, and none of these scholarly cues: an entry retrieved from a publisher or DOI address may be a journal article, so it stays unidentified.
_quality_quantifiers_note: What a quality level's own words say about the share of the list that is journal or conference papers or books (catalogue-confirmed or typed from the citation text). A reading's level is accepted only when the share holds however the unidentified and other entries turn out: above min_share at the lowest possible share, below max_share at the highest. A level whose words match none of these cannot be checked against the counts, so it is not accepted.
_wording_note: Every sentence this step writes on a criterion row. {placeholders} are filled from the counts. Entries typed from citation text as web pages are only ever information: they may be journal articles retrieved online, so they never decide a level.

wording.counts: Reference list of {entries} entries: {major} journal or conference papers and books{from_text}, {web} that appear to be web sources, {repositories}{other}and {unclassified} of unknown type.
wording.counts_from_text: ({n} of them classified from how the entry is written)
wording.counts_lookup_unavailable: {n} of those could not be looked up because a catalogue was unreachable; a later check may identify them.
wording.web_note: Every level, including the lowest, allows at most {limit} internet sites, and {web} entries appear to be web sources. Decide whether they count as internet sites under this format, then choose a grade.
wording.inventory_short: Even counting every entry a catalogue did not confirm as a major reference, no level of this format fits these counts, so VERIDICAL did not choose one. Please check the reference list.
wording.inventory_open: Only entries a catalogue confirmed can count against the list, so these counts allow anything from {low} to {high}. The rest of each level's wording, such as how many formatting errors there are, is not something the counts show, so VERIDICAL did not choose one.
wording.inventory_ungraded: The counts fit one level, but the formatting part of this criterion was not graded automatically. Please check the reference list.
wording.inventory_lowered: These counts allow no higher level than this one, so the grader's higher level for the formatting was lowered to it.
wording.inventory_same: These counts allow this level, and the formatting was graded the same.
wording.inventory_formatting: The counts would allow a higher level; the formatting grade sets this one.
wording.quality_none: These counts do not confirm any one level's wording however the entries a catalogue did not confirm turn out, so VERIDICAL did not choose one. Please check the reference list.
wording.quality_several: These counts fit more than one level ({levels}); what separates them is not something the counts show, so VERIDICAL did not choose one. Please check the reference list.
wording.quality_decided: Only this level's wording fits these counts, however the entries a catalogue did not confirm turn out.
wording.no_entries: No reference entries were available to judge.
wording.problem_not_finished: The citation check did not finish, so the reference list could not be judged.
wording.problem_selection: VERIDICAL could not separate the reference list reliably, so it could not be counted or judged. Please check the reference list.
wording.problem_empty: No reference list was found to count or judge. Please check the manuscript.
wording.problem_unread_pages: Some pages could not be read (pages {pages}), so the reference list may be incomplete and was not counted or judged. Please check the reference list.
wording.problem_boundary: VERIDICAL could not confirm where the reference list starts and ends, so it was not counted or judged. Please check the reference list.
wording.problem_partial: The citation check could not read the whole reference list, so it was not counted or judged. Please check the reference list.
wording.entries_to_check: Entries to check, by their place in the reference list: {numbers}.
wording.quality_share: Between {low} and {high} of the {entries} entries can be journal or conference papers or books.
